deep_reading.architecture_zh: 系统分为 root 和 leaf 两部分：root 维护大型内存特征缓存，负责特征获取、预处理和请求扇出；leaf 按分区组织模型，每个分区托管一组相关模型（如一个生产模型和多个实验变体）。Feature Trimmer 是在 root 主机内运行的模块，加载按 model name + version 索引的特征 allowlist 映射，在 root 向 leaf 扇出请求时只保留各模型实际需要的特征。签名映射以 model signature（module_info.json）为源，由 bundle 构建流水线聚合成 bundle 级 artifact，随 root 配置通过 canary、ACA、prod、rollback 等同一部署流程下发到 root 主机。Trimmer 内部维护独立 bundle 映射和合并后的只读映射，使用 shared/unique lock 管理并发读写，并在文件内容变化时触发重新加载和原子替换。
business_implications_zh: 通过降低 root-leaf 网络用量，Pinterest 得以缩减 root 集群规模（Ads 27%、Homefeed 33%），并可将 root 从网络优化型 m6in 换到约便宜 20% 的 m6i 实例
项目实现超过 $4M 年化基础设施成本节省，并额外产生约 $0.98M 的集群权利润化收益
网络瓶颈解除为更大模型和更多实验提供 headroom，避免延迟或网络性能成为业务增长的约束
延迟改善降低了服务端超时导致的失败，带来约 0.17% 的边际收入增长，说明基础设施优化可直接转化为业务收益
团队通过有意识地在延迟 headroom 与成本之间做 tradeoff，将优化收益的一部分用于节省成本，一部分用于未来实验，展示了成本治理的务实路径

evidence_refs.heading: Enable compression to reduce network usage

deep_reading.implementation_zh: 实现要点包括：(1) 每个模型训练完成后将 model signature 导出为 module_info.json，放在 .pt 归档中或作为独立 artifact；(2) bundle 构建时迭代各模型版本，解析 module_info.json 生成 bundle 级 mapping，缺失签名时记录 warning 并跳过而不阻断构建；(3) root 配置先于 leaf 模型版本部署，allowlist 按 model name + version 键控，未匹配时跳过 trimming 以避免 stale config；(4) Feature Trimmer 模块启动时加载各 bundle 的 module_info.json 到独立内存 map，通过文件 watcher 监听更新，再合并为新的 consolidated map 并原子替换；(5) 查找逻辑：未找到模型 allowlist 则不裁剪；指定 version 且命中则使用该版本；模型名命中但版本缺失或未命中则回退到最新版本 allowlist；(6) 初始化失败不阻断 host 启动，只发告警；单个 bundle 文件损坏时保留旧内存版本，不影响其他 bundle 更新。
lessons_zh: 压缩是快速但有限的早期胜利，真正有效的是停止发送未使用的数据，即 'Send What You Use' 原则
将 model signature 作为模型所需特征的唯一事实来源，并以轻量 artifact 形式随训练流程发布，是实现同步的关键
让 trimmer 配置与模型部署走同一套 staged delivery 和 rollback 机制，可以避免手工维护脆弱配置
allowlist 比 blocklist 更适合快速演进的 ML 特征生态，因为不需要追踪所有可能新增或废弃的特征
按模型名+版本做 allowlist 查找并回退到最新版本，配合 signature 跨版本一致性假设，可大幅简化滚动部署期间的内存和配置管理
将各 bundle 的签名映射隔离加载，可让单个 bundle 文件损坏或部署失败时不拖累其他 bundle 的裁剪能力
limitations_zh: 文章是 Pinterest 工程博客的自我报告，未提供第三方验证或完整实验对照
优化依赖 'model signature 在不同版本间保持一致' 这一强假设，若违反则需要 fork 新模型，约束了模型迭代方式
若模型没有有效 allowlist 或请求版本未命中，系统会跳过裁剪，相关模型仍保持原延迟峰值（文中 Related Pins 部分模型如此）
结果指标（网络、延迟、成本、收入提升）均为 Pinterest 特定环境数据，迁移到其他系统时可能因架构、实例类型、特征规模和流量模式不同而有所差异
文中提到 root cluster 的瓶颈从网络转移到 CPU，说明该方案并非无成本，后续需要继续优化 CPU 或 SerDe 开销
文章仅覆盖 root-leaf 段优化；client-root 段的请求特征压缩留待 Part II，因此本文不包含端到端完整结论
production_constraints_zh: root 必须精确知道每个 leaf 模型当前版本所需的特征列表，而模型每小时到每天频繁刷新，且多个模型以 bundle 形式一起上线
模型 rollout 采用 canary、automated canary analysis、prod、rollback 等分阶段流程，trimmer 配置必须与模型部署同步且可回滚
要求模型的 signature 在不同版本间保持一致；如需新增输入特征必须 fork 新模型，以支撑 versioned lookup 的 fallback 机制
Feature Trimmer 处于关键失败路径：裁剪失败会导致网络带宽突增甚至级联故障，因此必须处理 module_info.json 损坏或部署失败
压缩和裁剪都会增加 CPU 开销和潜在延迟，需要权衡网络节省与 CPU/延迟成本
allowlist 未覆盖或失效时系统选择跳过 trimming，会产生临时 rollout gap，因此需要向前兼容地同时包含当前和待发布版本的 allowlist
results_zh: lz4 压缩先降低了 20% root-leaf 网络用量，但未解决根本问题
Feature Trimmer 上线后，Ads root 集群峰值网络带宽从 4Gbps 降至 <1.5Gbps，且 root 集群规模还下调了 27%
Ads leaf 分区网络峰值从部分集群的 1000–1200 MBPS 降至所有集群 <200 MBPS
Homefeed root 出站网络从约 1.2–2.1 GB/s 降至约 0.45–1.1 GB/s，GPU leaf 集群入站网络降低 65–75%，Homefeed root 集群规模缩减 33%
Related Pins 模型 p99 延迟从约 130–180ms（常超 200ms）降至约 95–125ms，降幅约 25–30%；Ads client（AdMixer）p90 延迟从 >90ms 峰值降至 <80ms
Search 和 Notification 的 egress 网络吞吐分别下降约 45% 和 65%，在无 p99 延迟实质变化的情况下实现各自 ≥30% 成本降低
Search/Notification 权利润化带来额外约 $0.98M 年化基础设施成本节省，整体项目为 Pinterest 节省超过 $4M 年化基础设施成本
Ads 利用网络释放调整 batching 逻辑，改善 GPU 利用率，约相当于当时总 GPU 容量的 5%；延迟改善还带来约 0.17% 的边际收入提升
deep_reading.system_context_zh: Pinterest 的在线 ML 推理采用 root-leaf 架构：root 负责从特征存储获取特征、做预处理，并将打分请求扇出到多个 leaf 分区；leaf 使用 GPU 执行模型推理。由于 root 为减少特征存储 QPS 而缓存所有模型所需特征的并集，并通过网络把完整特征集发送给每个 leaf，root-leaf 之间的网络带宽成为在线服务瓶颈，系统不得不按网络用量而非算力扩容。Ads 场景中 leaf 峰值网络用量显著高于 GPU SM 活动，root 需要网络优化型 AWS m6in 实例才能满足 SLA。
tradeoffs_zh: 启用 fbthrift lz4 压缩带来约 20% root-leaf 网络用量下降，代价是 5% CPU 用量增加和约 5ms（约 10%）p90 延迟增加
Feature Trimmer 的 'Send What You Use' 相比压缩是更大的杠杆，用额外 CPU 工作换取约 50% 网络传输量减少的潜力
采用 allowlist 而非 blocklist：allowlist 无需追踪所有开发中或废弃特征，而 blocklist 规模更大且增长更快
在旧架构（同一 GPU host 同时做特征处理和推理）中传输未用特征只增加内存；新 root-leaf 架构中则成为显著网络开销，因此值得为裁剪增加 CPU 和部署复杂度
延迟改善带来的 headroom 被用来换取成本节省（trading some latency for cost），剩余 headroom 用于未来实验
项目最终把瓶颈从网络转移到 root 集群的 CPU 上，后续优化焦点转向 client 与 root 之间的 payload

excerpt: Guangtong Bai | Staff Software Engineer, Product ML Infrastructure*; Shantam Shorewala | Software Engineer II, Product ML Infrastructure*; Chi Zhang | Staff Software Engineer, AI Platform*; Neha Upadhyay | Software Engineer II, AI Platform*; Haoyang Li | Director, Product ML Infrastructure *These authors contributed equally to this article. Background At Pinterest, our online ML serving systems employ a root-leaf architecture. On a high level, the architecture looks as follows: Figure 1: Root-leaf Architecture of Online ML Serving Systems at Pinterest In the diagram, “Client Service” is responsible for recommending organic or promoted Pins to users. In order to know if a given Pin is relevant to a particular user request, client service sends a score request to the online ML serving system to have the Pin scored by a bunch of ML models, each of which scores an aspect of “relevancy”. The online ML serving system is composed of 2 parts: Root: This component handles initial feature processing. Its responsibilities include retrieving necessary features from the feature store, performing required preprocessing, and distributing (fanning out) the scoring requests to the various leaf partitions. Leaf: This is where the actual model inference takes place, typically utilizing GPU machines. It is structured into multiple partitions, each of which hosts a related group of models, such as one production model and several experimental variants. What is flowing between the services are ML features. In this blog, we share how passing too many features from root to leaf created a network bottleneck and how we resolved it with Feature Trimmer. Motivation The root-leaf architecture provides us with significant benefits, namely: Simplified Model Onboarding: New ML models can easily be onboarded for online serving by creating new leaf partitions, transparent to root and upstream clients. Reduced Feature Store QPS: The system minimizes RPCs to the feature store for fetching ML features by having all leaf partitions share a large in-memory feature cache in the root. Optimized Resource Utilization: Separating CPU (feature fetching, preprocessing) and GPU (model inference) workloads allows for optimized resource use, improving efficiency and reducing cost. However, this setup introduced a new challenge — the network bandwidth between root and leaf became a performance bottleneck on the online serving path; we had to scale the system based on network usage rather than compute . We observed this pressure in the Ads server on both the root and leaf partitions: On leaf partitions, peak network usage was significantly higher than peak GPU SM activity (see Figure 2). Consequently, the network bottleneck prevented us from fully utilizing the available GPU compute power. On root, we had to use the network optimized AWS instance type m6in to ensure the server latency met our internal SLA. Figure 2. Comparison of the network bandwidth usage vs GPU SM activity on a subset of the leaf partitions of the online ML server That led to a straightforward idea: reduce the root-leaf network bandwidth usage to unlock immediate fleet downscaling and infrastructure savings. If we could cut bandwidth enough, we could also move the root from network-optimized m6in instances to standard m6i instances (about 20% cheaper), further reducing cost. Enable compression to reduce network usage The most direct way to reduce the root-leaf network bandwidth usage is to compress the requests between them. This compression strategy is well-suited for the requests sent from the root to the leaf, which primarily carry ML features for multiple candidate Pins for a given user request. These requests are compressible for several reasons: Feature Set Consistency: The set of features requested is identical across different candidate Pins, although the actual feature values vary. summary_zh: 本文介绍 Pinterest 在线推荐系统采用的 root-leaf 在线 ML 服务架构，并针对 root 到 leaf 传递过多特征造成的网络带宽瓶颈，提出 Feature Trimmer 进行特征压缩，以降低带宽和成本、提高 GPU 利用率。
title: Optimizing ML Workload Network Efficiency (Part I): Feature Trimmer
